symptoms: Olive-green to black, scabby spots on leaves and fruit
Yellowing of leaves and premature leaf drop
Deformed or cracked fruit
organic_treatment: Apply neem oil or sulfur sprays
prevention: Clean up fallen leaves in autumn

symptoms: Purple spots on leaves that enlarge and turn brown with black centers (frog-eye leaf spot)
Dark brown to black rotting on fruit, often starting at the calyx end
Cankers on branches and trunks
organic_treatment: Prune out and destroy infected wood, leaves, and fruit
prevention: Remove dead wood and mummified fruit
Avoid mechanical injury to the tree

symptoms: Bright orange or yellow spots on leaves
Orange spots on fruit
Premature defoliation
causes: Requires both apple and juniper (cedar) hosts to complete life cycle
organic_treatment: Apply copper sprays before symptoms appear
Remove nearby juniper hosts if possible
prevention: Remove eastern red cedars within 1-2 miles

symptoms: White, powdery fungal growth on leaves and stems
Curled or distorted leaves
Stunted growth
Tan, rectangular lesions on leaves, restricted by leaf veins
Lesions may merge, causing extensive blighting
Reduced yield and poor ear fill
prevention: Crop rotation with non-host crops (e.g., soybeans)

symptoms: Circular to elongate, golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture to expose dusty spores
Yellowing and necrosis of leaves
organic_treatment: Rarely needed as most commercial hybrids are resistant
prevention: Early planting to avoid peak spore periods

symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green to tan lesions on leaves (cigar-shaped)
Lesions can merge, causing entire leaves to die
Starts on lower leaves and moves up
organic_treatment: Deep tillage to reduce crop residue

symptoms: Small, tan spots with dark margins on leaves
Berries turn brown, then shrivel into hard, black mummies
Small black dots (pycnidia) appear on infected tissues
organic_treatment: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves
prevention: Sanitation: remove all mummies from vines and ground

symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern on leaves (interveinal chlorosis and necrosis)
Small, dark spots on berries (measles)
Sudden vine wilting (apoplexy)
organic_treatment: Trunk renewal (retraining a sucker from the base)
chemical_treatment: Protect pruning wounds with registered sealants or fungicides (e.g., thiophanate-methyl)

symptoms: Irregular, dark reddish-brown to black spots on leaves
Spots may merge, causing large dead areas
Premature leaf drop
Mottled, asymmetrical yellowing of leaves
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit that remain green at the bottom
Twig dieback and overall tree decline
causes: Transmitted by the Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri)
organic_treatment: No cure exists. Infected trees must be removed and destroyed.
Control psyllid vectors using horticultural oils or soaps
chemical_treatment: Insecticides to control the Asian citrus psyllid (e.g., Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam)

symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots on leaves, turning purplish-black
Centers of leaf spots may fall out (shot-hole appearance)
Dark, sunken spots or cracks on fruit
causes: Favored by warm, wet, and windy conditions
organic_treatment: Apply copper sprays (with caution to avoid phytotoxicity)

symptoms: Small, brown, water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots turn necrotic with yellow halos
Scab-like, raised lesions on fruit
Defoliation
causes: Xanthomonas euvesicatoria, X. vesicatoria, X. perforans, or X. gardneri (bacteria)
chemical_treatment: Copper fungicides (often mixed with Mancozeb to reduce resistance)

symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like) on older leaves
Yellowing surrounding the spots
Dark, sunken lesions on tubers
organic_treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or Bacillus subtilis
prevention: Maintain adequate nitrogen and soil fertility

symptoms: Water-soaked, dark green to black spots on leaves, rapidly expanding
White fungal growth on the underside of leaves in humid conditions
Brown, dry rot on tubers
prevention: Destroy cull piles and volunteer potatoes
Prune out old canes after fruiting
Inoculate seeds with rhizobia if needed

symptoms: White, powdery fungal spots on leaves and stems
Leaves turn yellow and dry up
Reduced fruit size and quality
Irregular, dark purple to brown spots on leaves
Spots coalesce, causing the leaf to turn brown and dry up (scorch)
Lesions on runners, petioles, and fruit calyxes
organic_treatment: Improve air circulation and weed control

symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots become necrotic with yellow halos
Scab-like, raised lesions on fruit
Severe defoliation
causes: Xanthomonas vesicatoria, X. euvesicatoria, X. perforans, X. gardneri (bacteria)
organic_treatment: Copper sprays (mixed with mancozeb if possible)
prevention: Crop rotation (avoid planting tomatoes or peppers in the same spot for 2-3 years)

symptoms: Dark, concentric rings (target spots) on older leaves
Yellowing of leaves starting from the bottom of the plant
Dark, sunken lesions on the stem end of the fruit
causes: Alternaria linariae (formerly A. tomatophila) or Alternaria solani (fungus)
organic_treatment: Apply copper fungicides or Bacillus subtilis
prevention: Stake or cage plants to keep foliage off the ground

symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves, rapidly expanding
White fungal growth on leaf undersides in wet conditions
Firm, dark brown, greasy-looking spots on fruit
organic_treatment: Destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)

symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety fungal growth on the lower leaf surface
Leaves eventually curl, wither, and drop
causes: Favored by high humidity, especially in greenhouses
prevention: Water at the base of the plant

symptoms: Small, circular spots with dark borders and gray/tan centers on older leaves
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) in the center of the spots
Severe defoliation starting from the bottom up
Stippling or tiny yellow/white dots on leaves
Fine webbing visible on the undersides of leaves or between stems
Leaves turn yellow, bronze, and eventually dry and fall off
organic_treatment: Spray with a strong stream of water to wash them off
Insecticidal soaps or horticultural oils (neem oil)
prevention: Maintain adequate watering (drought stress increases susceptibility)
Keep the area free of weeds

symptoms: Small, dark spots on leaves that enlarge and develop concentric rings (target-like)
Sunken, dark lesions on the fruit with target-like rings
Leaf yellowing and drop
Severe stunting of the plant
Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins
Reduced fruit set and size
causes: Transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
organic_treatment: No cure for infected plants; they must be removed and destroyed
Control whiteflies with neem oil, insecticidal soap, or sticky traps
chemical_treatment: Insecticides to control whiteflies (e.g., Imidacloprid, Dinotefuran)
prevention: Use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies

symptoms: Mottling or mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves
Stunted growth
Fern-like or shoestring-like leaf distortion
Internal browning or uneven ripening of fruit
causes: Transmitted mechanically (tools, hands, clothing) and via seed
organic_treatment: No cure. Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Wash hands and disinfect tools thoroughly
chemical_treatment: None. Viruses cannot be treated with chemicals.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties (indicated by 'T' in the variety name)
Do not smoke around plants (tobacco mosaic virus is related)
Ensure proper nutrition (calcium to prevent blossom end rot)
